persona: observer-agent: a coding agent supervising a long tuning run on behalf of a human, needing machine-readable answers (health, progress, failures, best-so-far, budget) while the run is in progress, plus crash/resume behaviour. Windows 11, fake provider only.
journey: All work was done in $S (cwd for every command; PY = <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe). I read README.md, docs/new-experiment.md, AGENTS.md, examples/pyvrp/README.md and every --help (16:55), copied examples/binpacking into exp/, wrote slow_evaluate.py (sleeps 8-15 s, every 5th call exits 7 with a stderr message) and a 20-line evolvekit.slow.yaml using `extends`. `preflight` on it was clean in 33 s and projected 10.4 min. At 16:57:37 I started the run in the background via PowerShell Start-Process with stdout/stderr redirected (launcher pid 13628, real interpreter pid 7556 per .lock) and polled `status` every ~25 s from a second shell. For the first 45 s status said "no runs recorded"; afterwards it only moved at generation boundaries, never said alive/dead, planned generations, in-flight or failed evaluations, elapsed or ETA. The redirected stdout stayed at 0 bytes. At 17:00:41, mid generation 3 (evaluator child 11100 in flight), I ran taskkill /F /PID 13628; the whole tree died except the evaluator, which ran 10 s more. status was byte-identical before and after the kill, exit 0. Re-running the same command (with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 so I could see stdout) reclaimed the lock, said "resumed 7 candidate(s)", reused ids g003-c0008..10, overwrote their traces, re-bought the generation and then ran 6 MORE generations (to gen 8). A second concurrent run was refused cleanly with exit 3. Five of 29 evaluator calls failed; none appeared in stdout, status or the markdown leaderboard, and a candidate whose hold-out evaluation crashed became "best". With the unmodified fast evaluator I then tested caps: budget.max_usd resets on every resume (cum $0.0189 against a $0.0045 cap), and max_full_evals_per_day does not stop anything - it scores promoted candidates -1000. I never read evolvekit source. All processes I started have exited (verified). Note: at the end `git status` showed ` M docs/mission/DECISION_LOG.md` in the repo; I did not create or touch that file (other jobs run on this machine).

entries.title: budget.max_usd (and stop.patience) reset on every resume: the 'hard cost budget' is per process, not per run dir
entries.step: Find out whether the USD cap carries over when the same command is re-run against the same --run-dir (what a supervising agent does after a crash).
entries.command: exp/evolvekit.budget.yaml = `extends: evolvekit.yaml` + `budget: {max_usd: 0.0045, max_tokens: 500000, max_full_evals_per_day: 40}`; then three times: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit run --config exp/evolvekit.budget.yaml --run-dir runB --generations 2   (third time --generations 1). Control: same config, fresh dir: ... run --config exp/evolvekit.budget.yaml --run-dir runC
entries.observed: Run #1: `gen 2 ... spent=$0.0034`, `stop reason : generations exhausted`. Run #2 (cum already $0.0034 of $0.0045): `resumed 7 candidate(s)...`, `gen 3  3 child(ren) ... spent=$0.0025` / `economics  cum=$0.0059`, `gen 4  1 child(ren) ... spent=$0.0130` / `economics  cum=$0.0163`, `stop reason : generations exhausted`. Run #3 (cum $0.0163, 3.6x the cap): `gen 5  3 child(ren) ... spent=$0.0025`, `economics cum=$0.0189`, `spend : $0.0189 over 23 call(s)`, exit=0. Control runC in ONE session: `gen 3  2 child(ren) ... spent=$0.0046` / `stop reason : budget.max_usd reached: $0.0046 of $0.0045`. Also in runD (patience: 8 inherited) the best never moved from gen 1 to gen 13 across three sessions and patience never fired. The per-generation `spent=$` restarts from 0 on resume while the adjacent `economics cum=$` is cumulative.
entries.expected: A run dir whose usage.jsonl already totals more than budget.max_usd refuses to make another LLM call ('budget.max_usd reached: $0.0163 of $0.0045 (carried over from usage.jsonl)'). README: 'a USD cap that stops the run by itself', 'hard stops, not warnings', and step 6 'wait it out and re-run the same directory (the lock and the ledger resume cleanly)'.
entries.why_it_matters: A supervising agent's standard reaction to a crash or a provider halt is 're-run the same command'. Every restart silently grants a fresh max_usd/max_tokens/patience allowance, so a crash-looping or babysat run has no spending ceiling at all, and the human who set max_usd believes it has one.
entries.suggested_fix: Initialise the budget guard and the patience/plateau counters from usage.jsonl + runs.jsonl on resume; print the carried-over amounts in the 'resumed ...' line; make `spent=` cumulative (or label it 'this session').

entries.title: budget.max_full_evals_per_day is not a stop: once hit, every promoted candidate is scored failure_score (-1000) and archived, silently
entries.step: Check whether the full-evals-per-day cap carries over a resume.
entries.command: exp/evolvekit.evalcap.yaml = `extends: evolvekit.yaml` + `budget: {max_usd: 1.0, max_tokens: 500000, max_full_evals_per_day: 3}`; <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit run --config exp/evolvekit.evalcap.yaml --run-dir runD   (run twice, then once more with --generations 1); then parsed runD/runs.jsonl
entries.observed: The run never stops on the cap: run #1 went gen 1..6, `stop reason : generations exhausted`; run #2 went gen 7..12, `spent=$0.0776`; total `spend : $0.1225 over 90 call(s)`, best stuck at -5.61986. No line containing 'cap', 'per_day' or 'full eval' in stdout or in `status`. runs.jsonl: `g002-c0005 ['static','proxy'] score -1000.0 rank -1000.0 cell [3, 0] last_failure: 'stage full: daily full-evaluation cap reached'` (same for g002-c0007, g003-c0009, ...), rejected=false. In an uncapped run the identical g002-c0005 scores -5.72484, an improvement on the seed. The count itself did carry over the resume (ledger stayed at 3 full evals).
entries.expected: README: 'max_full_evals_per_day. A hard stop, not a warning'. Either the run halts with `stop reason : budget.max_full_evals_per_day reached`, or it waits for the next day; a candidate that was never evaluated must not be recorded with failure_score or inserted into the archive.
entries.why_it_matters: This is the cap the README recommends as 'the real cap' for hour-long evaluators. After it is hit the run keeps buying LLM children that can never be promoted, records its most promising candidates as -1000 failures (and the structural duplicate filter will then reject a re-proposal of the same block), and nothing in stdout/status tells the supervisor.
entries.suggested_fix: Make it an actual stop (or a documented sleep-until-window). If promotion is skipped, keep the proxy score, mark the row `deferred: cap`, do not archive it at failure_score, and re-queue it on the next resume. Print the counter (`full evals today 3/3`) in the gen line and in `status`.

entries.title: `status` cannot tell running from crashed from finished; identical output and exit 0 after taskkill; stop reason is persisted nowhere
entries.step: Answer 'is the run healthy (running / stalled / crashed)?' before and after hard-killing my run (taskkill /F /PID 13628 at 17:00:41, mid generation 3).
entries.command: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit status --run-dir run1   (at 17:00:40 alive, at 17:00:54 dead, at 17:04:50 finished)
entries.observed: Alive and dead outputs are identical: `candidates : 7 (2 rejected)` ... `generations : 2` / `archive : no archive.json snapshot yet` / `best : g002-c0005 rank=-5.72484 ...` / `spend : $0.0050`, `status exit=0`. run1/.lock still read `{"pid": 7556, "host": "Delius", "started": "2026-09-19T14:57:38+00:00"}` with pid 7556 gone. After the resumed run completed, status shows no 'finished' state or stop reason; `grep -rl exhausted run1` finds nothing, so `stop reason : generations exhausted` exists only in the process's stdout.
entries.expected: A first line such as `state : running (pid 7556, 3m02s, last write 12s ago)` / `dead (lock owner pid 7556 not alive; last write 17:00:09)` / `finished: generations exhausted at 17:04:40`, and a distinct exit code for a dead owner. The run already knows how to detect a dead lock owner (it prints 'reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 7556' on resume).
entries.why_it_matters: Liveness is the first question a supervisor asks every poll. Today the agent must parse .lock itself and call tasklist, and cannot learn why a run ended unless it captured stdout.
entries.suggested_fix: Have `status` read .lock, test the pid, print state + last-write age, and exit non-zero when the owner is dead. Write a `run_state.json` (state, stop_reason, session count, started/ended) at start, each generation and exit.

entries.title: Progress is only visible at generation boundaries: no in-flight/done/failed evaluation counts, no planned generations, no elapsed/ETA; 'no runs recorded' for the first 45 s
entries.step: Every ~25 s: which generation of how many, how many evaluations done / in flight / failed, elapsed and ETA.
entries.command: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit status --run-dir run1   (polled by poll.sh; run started 16:57:37)
entries.observed: 16:57:49 and 16:58:09: `no runs recorded in ...\run1` exit 0 (run alive, 3 evaluator calls done). 16:58:35 and 16:59:01: `candidates : 1 (0 rejected)` / `generations : 0` although evaluator call 5 had crashed at 16:58:44. All three gen-1 rows landed in runs.jsonl together at 16:59:05. Resumed run: 17:02:11 and 17:02:36 both `generations : 3`, runs.jsonl rows 10 -> 10 while evaluator calls went 18 -> 20. status never prints planned generations, evaluations done/in flight/failed, elapsed, ETA, patience counter, or budget remaining. The only live signal is file mtimes under run1/work/stage_out/, a directory the README's run-dir list does not mention.
entries.expected: runs.jsonl (or an events.jsonl) appended per candidate/stage as it completes, and status lines like `generation : 3 of 6 (child 2/3, stage full, g003-c0010, running 9s)`, `evaluations : 14 done, 1 in flight, 3 failed`, `elapsed 3m04s, ~7m left`.
entries.why_it_matters: With the 8-15 s evaluator status is 45-70 s stale; with examples/pyvrp (120 s proxy + 3 x 900 s full per promoted candidate, '70-80 minutes' per generation) the supervisor is blind for over an hour at a time and sees 'no runs recorded' for ~47 minutes after launch.
entries.suggested_fix: Append a row/event per stage completion, write a small heartbeat file (current candidate, stage, started_at), and surface planned vs completed generations and evaluation counts in status.

entries.title: Run stdout is block-buffered when redirected: 0 bytes for the whole session, and everything it printed is lost on a hard kill
entries.step: Run in the background with stdout/stderr redirected to files (the only way an agent can run it) and compare stdout with `status`.
entries.observed: Every poll from 16:58:09 to the kill at 17:00:41: `--- stdout log: 0 bytes`. After taskkill: `stdout log bytes: 0   stderr log bytes: 0` although two generations had completed. Re-launching with `$env:PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1"` (not mentioned anywhere in README/docs/--help) made the same lines appear live.
entries.expected: The run flushes each progress line (or writes `<run_dir>/run.log` itself), so a redirected log is never staler than the last generation and survives a crash.
entries.why_it_matters: Without the undocumented env var, `status` is the only signal and the gen lines, breadth decisions and the final `stop reason` are lost entirely if the process dies. The task asked how stale status is versus stdout: by default stdout is infinitely staler.
entries.suggested_fix: print(..., flush=True) / sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True) in the run loop, and tee progress to <run_dir>/run.log. Mention `python -u` in the README's 'Running for real'.

entries.title: Evaluator failures are invisible: 5 of 29 evaluator calls crashed and stdout, `status` and the markdown leaderboard never mention one
entries.step: Which evaluations failed, with what error, for which candidate and input?
entries.command: grep -ciE "exit code|fail|error|license|crash" run1b.stdout.log ; <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit status --run-dir run1 ; ... -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir run1 --html board2.html > board2.md ; grep -ciE "fail|exit code" board2.md
entries.observed: stdout grep count: `0`. `evaluator failures that actually happened: 5 of 29 calls`. status has no failure line. board2.md grep: `0`; it shows `| 5 | g001-c0004 | 1 | -1000 | -1000 | 3,0 | rewrite | ...` with no reason. Only runs.jsonl has it: `"last_failure": "stage proxy: exit code 7\nslow_evaluate: simulated solver crash on call 5: license server unreachable (FRICTION-TEST)"` (the HTML dashboard does embed last_failure). For a crashed hold-out call the text is `stage full: exit code 7 ...` - it does not say the failing input set was `holdout`, nor the seed or command line.
entries.expected: A stdout line per failed stage (`g001-c0004: stage proxy FAILED exit 7: license server unreachable`), a `failed evals : 5 (proxy 2, full 1, full/private 2)` line in status and the run summary, and the input set / seed in last_failure.
entries.why_it_matters: A 17-20 % infrastructure failure rate is exactly what a supervisor must escalate to the human; here it is indistinguishable from 'the LLM wrote bad code' unless the agent hand-parses an undocumented field.
entries.suggested_fix: Log stage failures as they happen, count them in status/summary/leaderboard, and include inputs, seed and the rendered command in last_failure.

entries.title: A crashed hold-out evaluation silently drops the hold-out penalty, and that candidate became the run's 'best'
entries.step: Best-so-far versus the seed, and how trustworthy that number is.
entries.command: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit status --run-dir run1   (17:04:11) and parsing run1/runs.jsonl
entries.observed: status: `best : g005-c0014 rank=-5.71704 score=-5.71704 cell=[3, 1]`. stdout: `gen 5  4 child(ren)  best=-5.71704` / `breadth 4 -> 3 (shrink: 1 improving generation(s); floor 3)`. runs.jsonl for g005-c0014: `pub -5.717 priv None rank -5.717`, `last_failure: 'stage full: exit code 7 ... simulated solver crash on call 25'` (call 25 was `--inputs holdout`). Same pattern for g004-c0011. The leaderboard shows `-` in the gap column with no flag.
entries.expected: A candidate whose private evaluation failed is either retried, ranked as unverified (not eligible for 'best'), or flagged like the `!` hold-out flag. ranking = public - penalty x max(0, public - private) should not quietly become ranking = public.
entries.why_it_matters: The README's hold-out section exists because a past winner 'improved the public set and its hold-out went backwards'. A flaky evaluator re-opens that hole, and the unverified candidate also reset the plateau/breadth logic as an 'improvement'.
entries.suggested_fix: Treat a failed private run as a failed stage for ranking (or retry once); flag `private: failed` in status/leaderboard; exclude such rows from `best`.

entries.title: A transient evaluator failure is charged to the candidate forever: no retry, score -1000, still inserted into an archive cell
entries.step: See how a 1-in-5 infrastructure failure (non-zero exit + stderr, no output file) is handled.
entries.command: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit run --config exp\evolvekit.slow.yaml --run-dir run1   then parsing run1/runs.jsonl; comparison run with the unmodified evaluator: ... run --config exp/evolvekit.budget.yaml --run-dir runB --generations 2
entries.observed: run1: `g001-c0004 gen 1 ok ['static'] score -1000.0 ... rank -1000.0 cell [3, 0]`, rejected=false, last_failure 'stage proxy: exit code 7 ...'. In runB the same scripted child g001-c0004 scores `-5.61986`, the first improvement of that run. The evaluator log shows exactly one call for it (call=5); it was never re-run. g002-c0007 same. I did not observe a later re-proposal being rejected as a duplicate of it, so that consequence is unverified.
entries.expected: A configurable retry for stage crashes (exit code/timeout with no KPI file), or at least an 'infra failure' verdict that keeps the candidate out of the archive and eligible for re-evaluation on resume.
entries.why_it_matters: On a long run with a flaky solver/licence/cluster, a fifth of the paid candidates are destroyed, including real improvements; the README only says 'a crash below stage 0 is evaluate.failure_score' and offers no knob.
entries.suggested_fix: Add `evaluate.stages[].retries` (default 1 for non-zero exit without an output file), distinguish `evaluator_error` from a candidate-caused failure, and do not archive evaluator_error rows.

entries.title: Resume reuses candidate ids: traces overwritten, stale candidate/stage_out files under the same id, per-candidate usd double-attributed
entries.step: After the hard kill, resume with the same command and check ids, traces and usage accounting.
entries.command: Copy-Item -Recurse run1 run1.crashsnap ; (resume) ; md5sum run1.crashsnap/traces/g003-c0009.json run1/traces/g003-c0009.json ; md5sum of work/candidates/g003-c0009.py in both ; python script grouping run1/usage.jsonl by candidate_id and ts
entries.observed: Resumed stdout: `g003-c0008 duplicate after 2 attempt(s)...`, `g003-c0009 duplicate ...`, `g003-c0010 duplicate ...` - the same three ids the killed session had already issued. Traces: `g003-c0009.json: snap=8cac4ae7 now=6d14ed26` (all three overwritten). `work/candidates/g003-c0009.py: snap=b29b8e80 now=b29b8e80` and stage_out `g003-c0009.proxy.json`, `g003-c0010.full.json` remain from the DEAD session although runs.jsonl now says g003-c0009 is a never-evaluated duplicate. usage.jsonl gen 3 has 10 rows under 3 ids from two sessions; runs.jsonl `g003-c0009 usd= 0.00123` = crashed-session 0.000407 + resumed-session 0.000823. Totals are right (sum usage $0.045616), attribution is not.
entries.expected: Ids are never reissued (continue the counter from usage.jsonl/traces, or add a session suffix); the orphaned partial generation is recorded as such; stale work files are removed or quarantined.
entries.why_it_matters: An agent asked 'what did g003-c0009 cost / look like' gets source code and KPIs of a different program than the ledger row, the trace of four paid calls is gone, and `preflight --candidate run1/work/candidates/g003-c0009.py` would test the wrong candidate.
entries.suggested_fix: Seed the id counter from max(id) over runs.jsonl, usage.jsonl and traces/; write `abandoned` rows for ids with usage but no runs row; include a session id in usage rows.

entries.title: Hard kill mid-generation loses the whole generation (paid LLM calls + finished evaluations) and the resume message does not say so
entries.step: Inspect the run dir after taskkill in the middle of generation 3's evaluations; then resume.
entries.command: taskkill /F /PID 13628   (my launcher; its child 7556 was the lock owner) ; then parsing run1/runs.jsonl + run1/usage.jsonl ; then re-running the same run command
entries.observed: runs.jsonl ended at g002-c0007 (7 rows, all parseable, no torn line). usage.jsonl already had 4 generation-3 rows ($0.0017 of $0.0050 = 34 % of spend). work/stage_out held finished results g003-c0009.proxy.json, g003-c0010.proxy.json (+ g003-c0010.full.json written 10 s after the kill by the orphaned evaluator). Resume printed only `reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 7556` / `resumed 7 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl (3/16 cells occupied ...)` and then bred a brand-new generation 3 with 6 new LLM calls; nothing mentions the discarded 4 calls / 4 evaluations. No archive.json existed (it is only written at the end of a run; status said `archive : no archive.json snapshot yet` for the whole run).
entries.expected: Per-candidate rows written as each candidate finishes, so a resume keeps evaluated children and only redoes the in-flight one; and a line such as `discarded partial generation 3: 4 LLM call(s) $0.0017, 3 finished stage result(s)`.
entries.why_it_matters: Here it was ~45 s and a fraction of a cent; on examples/pyvrp it is up to an hour of solver time plus paid calls, re-bought silently. docs/new-experiment.md promises 'resume cleanly ... pick up where they left off'.
entries.suggested_fix: Checkpoint at candidate granularity (append the runs.jsonl row when a candidate's cascade ends), reuse stage_out files whose candidate hash matches, snapshot archive.json each generation, and report what was discarded on resume.

entries.title: `generations` means 'N more' on resume: a 6-generation run that crashed in gen 3 ran to gen 8; --generations has no help text
entries.step: Which generation is it in and how many are planned?
entries.command: (resume) <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit run --config exp\evolvekit.slow.yaml --run-dir run1 ; C:\...\python.exe -m evolvekit run --help
entries.observed: Config has `search.generations: 6`. Session 1 completed gens 1-2 and died in 3; the resumed session printed `gen 3` ... `gen 8` then `stop reason : generations exhausted`. runD with the same config re-run: `gen 7` ... `gen 12`. Help: `--generations GENERATIONS` and `--quiet` with no description. The run dir records neither the config path nor the planned count.
entries.expected: Either generations is a run-level total (resume does the remaining 4) or the docs/help say 'additional generations per invocation'; the resume line should state the plan (`resuming at generation 3, will run to 8`).
entries.why_it_matters: A supervisor cannot compute 'N of M' or an ETA, and the projected wall clock from preflight (10.4 min for 6 generations) is silently exceeded after every restart.
entries.suggested_fix: Document the semantics in --help and README, print the target generation on start/resume, and store config path + hash + planned generations in the run dir.

entries.title: No machine-readable status: no --json on status/leaderboard; runs.jsonl schema and the work/ directory are undocumented
entries.step: Is any of it available as JSON?
entries.observed: `usage: python -m evolvekit status [-h] [--run-dir RUN_DIR]` - nothing else. leaderboard offers only `--limit` and `--html PATH`. I answered most questions by hand-parsing runs.jsonl (36 keys per row; README names about six of them) and usage.jsonl. `work/candidates` and `work/stage_out` are absent from the README's run-directory list, and preflight --help says candidates are 'saved under a run's candidates/ directory' while the real path is `<run_dir>/work/candidates/`.
entries.expected: `status --json` (state, pid, generation, planned, evals done/in flight/failed, best, seed, improvement %, spend vs caps, stop_reason) and a documented row schema.
entries.why_it_matters: An agent has to scrape aligned text whose labels can change, or reverse-engineer the ledger; every supervisor will re-implement the same fragile parser.
entries.suggested_fix: Add `--json` to status and leaderboard, document runs.jsonl/usage.jsonl/archive.json fields and the work/ layout in the README, fix the preflight help path.

entries.title: `status` contradicts itself mid-generation: 'generations : N' but the economics table already has an unmarked partial row N+1
entries.step: Which generation is the run in?
entries.observed: 16:59:15: `generations  : 1` followed by table rows `0`, `1` and `   2      9     0.0033       -5.871 ...`. 17:04:11: `generations  : 6` with a row `   7     38     0.0247     -5.71704           .       0.0036    $0.7228/unit`. The extra row comes from usage.jsonl (appended per LLM call) while candidates come from runs.jsonl (appended per generation); its 'best' and '$ since imp' are provisional but unmarked.
entries.expected: `generation : 7 in progress (6 complete)` and the partial row marked (e.g. `7*`).
entries.why_it_matters: Two different answers to 'which generation?' in one output; an agent scraping the last table row reports a best/$-per-unit figure for a generation that has not been scored yet.
entries.suggested_fix: Label completed vs in-progress explicitly and mark or omit the partial economics row.

entries.title: `status` on a mistyped/nonexistent run dir creates the directory and exits 0 with 'no runs recorded'; default run dir is undocumented
entries.step: Poll a run dir by path from a second shell.
entries.command: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit status --run-dir does-not-exist ; ls -la does-not-exist ; C:\...\python.exe -m evolvekit status
entries.observed: `no runs recorded in ...\observer-agent\does-not-exist` / `exit=0`; afterwards `does-not-exist/traces/` exists. Without --run-dir: `no runs recorded in ...\observer-agent\runs\latest`, exit 0, and `runs/latest/` was created in my cwd. `leaderboard --run-dir does-not-exist`: `No scored candidates yet.` exit 0. --help shows no default for --run-dir.
entries.expected: A read-only command never writes; a missing directory is `error: no such run directory` with a non-zero exit; --help shows `(default: runs/latest)`.
entries.why_it_matters: The same message and exit code cover 'typo', 'run has not written its seed yet' and 'empty dir', so a supervisor cannot alert on a wrong path, and stray directories appear wherever status is invoked.
entries.suggested_fix: Do not mkdir in status/leaderboard; exit 2 when the dir is missing; show defaults in argparse help.

entries.title: Hard-killed run leaves its in-flight evaluator subprocess running
entries.step: Check the process tree after taskkill /F on my run.
entries.observed: Before: child `11100 python.exe  python slow_evaluate.py --candidate ...g003-c0010.py --inputs full ...`. Kill at 17:00:41 took down 13628 and 7556. Evaluator log: `17:00:41 call=16 pid=11100 sleep=9.4` ... `17:00:51 call=16 done rc=120`, and run1/work/stage_out/g003-c0010.full.json has mtime 17:00:51 - the evaluator outlived the run by 10 s and wrote into the run dir.
entries.expected: Evaluator children die with the run (Windows job object with kill-on-close / POSIX process group), or the resume detects and reports still-running evaluators.
entries.why_it_matters: With the 900 s PyVRP solver an orphan burns a core for 15 minutes while the resumed run evaluates beside it - the README itself warns that 'CPU contention silently becomes solution quality'. It also writes into a run dir another process now owns.
entries.suggested_fix: Spawn stage commands in a job object / new process group tied to the run; record the evaluator pid in a heartbeat file so resume can check for it.

entries.title: Main README never says which interpreter or working directory a stage command runs with
entries.step: Wrap the example evaluator in my own script and reference it from the config as `python slow_evaluate.py ...`.
entries.observed: The run was `python3.13.exe` (the venv), its evaluator child was `python.exe  python slow_evaluate.py ...` resolved from PATH = `/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python312/python` (3.12). It worked only because the evaluator is stdlib-only. The relative script path resolved against the config's directory, which README/new-experiment.md do not state for commands (only for problem.skeleton). The explanation exists only in examples/pyvrp/README.md section 6.
entries.expected: One sentence in 'Adding a problem' step 3: commands run with cwd = the config's directory, and a bare `python` is the system interpreter on Windows, not the venv; offer a `{python}` placeholder.
entries.why_it_matters: An evaluator with third-party dependencies fails or silently runs under a different Python than the one preflighted in the user's head.
entries.suggested_fix: Document cwd and interpreter resolution in the main README and add a `{python}` (sys.executable) placeholder.

entries.title: `run` exits 0 for every stop reason, and the 'rejected' breakdown does not add up
entries.step: Decide programmatically why a run ended and read its summary.
entries.command: <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m evolvekit run --config exp/evolvekit.budget.yaml --run-dir runC ; echo exit=$?   and the final summary of run1
entries.observed: `stop reason : budget.max_usd reached: $0.0046 of $0.0045` -> `exit=0`; `stop reason : generations exhausted` -> `exit=0`. run1 summary: `rejected    : 17 (3 no-op, 8 duplicate, 2 behavioural)` (13 of 17; the 4 static / could-not-apply rejections are not itemised). Only the lock refusal has its own code (3, documented).
entries.expected: Documented distinct exit codes (or a machine-readable stop_reason file) for budget / patience / target / generations / provider-halt, and a breakdown that sums to the total.
entries.why_it_matters: A wrapper cannot tell 'finished as planned' from 'ran out of money' without scraping stdout, which by default is block-buffered.
entries.suggested_fix: Map stop reasons to exit codes as preflight already does (0/1/2), persist stop_reason, add `other` (static, unappliable) to the rejected breakdown.

unanswered_questions: Is the run alive, stalled, crashed or finished right now? status has no state line; I had to parse .lock and call tasklist myself, and I could not distinguish a slow evaluator from a hung one (no heartbeat; I did not test a true hang).
If it finished, why did it stop? The stop reason is printed only to stdout and persisted nowhere in the run dir.
How many generations are planned/remaining? Not in status, not in the run dir (the config path/hash is not recorded), and the meaning changes on resume (N more).
Which candidate, stage and input set is being evaluated right now, since when, and how many children of this generation are still queued?

How many evaluations are done / in flight / failed, and what is the failure rate per stage? Only derivable by hand from runs.jsonl last_failure; a failed hold-out call is not distinguishable from a failed public call.
Elapsed wall clock across sessions and an ETA against the stopping criteria: current patience counter, USD and tokens remaining against the caps, full evals used today against max_full_evals_per_day.
Seed baseline and % improvement mid-run: status prints only `best`; seed score and absolute improvement appear only in the end-of-run summary.
How noisy is the best score? With seeds: 1 kpi_cv is {} for every row, so there is no noise estimate at all (documented, but leaves the question open).
How does the current best differ from the seed? No command prints a candidate's block or a diff; I had to use the undocumented `block` field in runs.jsonl / work/candidates/<id>.py and diff myself.
Was this run dir resumed, how many times, and what was discarded each time (LLM calls, finished stage results)?
Is budget.max_usd / max_tokens / patience meant to be cumulative across resumes? Docs imply yes ('the ledger resumes cleanly'); observed behaviour is a reset.
What is a candidate's true cost after a resume, given ids are reused and usage rows from two sessions share an id?
Are evaluations ever run in parallel, and does the stage command inherit cwd/interpreter from the config dir or the caller? (Main README is silent; only examples/pyvrp/README.md hints.)
Is there a JSON form of `status`/`leaderboard`? (No flag exists; is the runs.jsonl schema stable enough to build on?)
went_well: preflight on my own slow/flaky config worked first time (33 s), printed per-stage durations, KPIs and evaluator notes, and its projection ('about 10.4min') was realistic; exit code 0/1/2 contract is documented.

The run lock behaves exactly as documented: a second run against the live dir exited 3 with `error: run directory ... is locked by pid 6584 (started 2026-09-19T15:01:44+00:00). Point --run-dir somewhere else, or wait ... If you are sure it is gone, delete ...\.lock` - clear, names the pid and the remedy, and did not disturb the first run.
Stale lock recovery needed no manual cleanup and says so: `reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 7556`, followed by `resumed 7 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl (3/16 cells occupied ...)`.
Hard kill did not corrupt the ledger: runs.jsonl and usage.jsonl parsed cleanly (no torn line) and the archive was rebuilt from runs.jsonl as the README promises.

runs.jsonl rows are rich and machine-readable once discovered: last_failure carries the stage, exit code and the evaluator's stderr text; lineage, stage_scores, cell, novelty verdicts, block source are all there. usage.jsonl is appended per LLM call in real time.
Cumulative totals survive a resume: `status` spend and the final `spend : $0.0456 over 45 call(s)` include the crashed session's calls.
In a single session budget.max_usd does stop the run with an exact message: `stop reason : budget.max_usd reached: $0.0046 of $0.0045`.
`extends` made my slow-evaluator variant a 20-line file, and the fake provider let me do the whole study (kill, resume, caps) with no keys and no network.
The HTML dashboard does include last_failure text for failed candidates (the markdown leaderboard and status do not).

On Windows, taskkill /F on the venv launcher pid that Start-Process returned also terminated the real interpreter (the lock-owner pid), so the pid an agent naturally records is sufficient to stop the run.
